summary:
Our project is a presentation designed to showcase analog base establishments based on similar terrestrial features.

This work indirectly addresses the 'Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars' challenge presented by NASA. To overcome this challenge, we utilized official resources such as NASA Earthdata Search and the NASA Planetary Data System to create a clear, accessible presentation that anyone can read and learn from.

This work is of great importance as it demystifies complex scientific processes and allows curious citizens to easily grasp the subject. Ultimately, our project creates sustainable educational value for young and old alike while making a tangible contribution to public scientific literacy.
details: Our project is an educational presentation designed to showcase analog base establishments on Earth for future space habitats. It works by visually mapping out specific terrestrial locations on Earth that share similar geographical, geological, or atmospheric features with permanent Moon and Mars base sites. By combining official NASA datasets with clean visual design, it translates complex planetary science and space architecture into an easy-to-digest format for everyone. The main benefit of our project is making space exploration and the idea of living on the Moon or Mars super easy to understand for everyone. Instead of confusing scientific reports, we bring it down to earth—literally showing how places right here on our planet share features with future space bases. Our goal is to spark curiosity, make space science fun, and show people of all ages that exploring other worlds starts right here at home. To create our presentation focusing on Moon and Mars base analogs, we utilized official NASA resources including NASA Earthdata Search and the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) for accurate data gathering and verification regarding base location criteria. For design and layout, we used professional graphic design software (Canva). Our project stands out in creativity by translating dense scientific datasets into an engaging, visually compelling presentation about Moon and Mars bases that appeals to young and old alike. Our team carefully considered factors such as scientific accuracy, visual hierarchy, and universal accessibility.
